entries.title: Isaiah 64:2
segments: 2. Oh, that Thy wrath would consume Thy foes as the fire. Rather, "as the fire burneth the dry brushwood" [GESENIUS].

entries.title: Isaiah 64:3

, translates from a different Hebrew root, "quake ... quaked"; but "fire" melts and causes to flow, rather than to quake (

entries.title: Isaiah 64:4
segments: 4. perceived by the ear--Paul (

) has for this, "nor have entered into the heart of man"; the virtual sense, sanctioned by his inspired authority; men might hear with the outward ear, but they could only by the Spirit "perceive" with the "heart" the spiritual significancy of God's acts, both those in relation to Israel, primarily referred to here, and those relating to the Gospel secondarily, which Paul refers to. 
 
    O God ... what he ... prepared--rather, "nor hath eye seen a god beside thee who doeth such things." They refer to God's past marvellous acts in behalf of Israel as a plea for His now interposing for His people; but the Spirit, as Paul by inspiration shows, contemplated further God's revelation in the Gospel, which abounds in marvellous paradoxes never before heard of by carnal ear, not to be understood by mere human sagacity, and when foretold by the prophets not fully perceived or credited; and even after the manifestation of Christ not to be understood save through the inward teaching of the Holy Ghost. These are partly past and present, and partly future; therefore Paul substitutes "prepared" for "doeth," though his context shows he includes all three. For "waiteth" he has "love Him"; godly waiting on Him must flow from love, and not mere fear.

entries.title: Isaiah 64:5
segments: 5. meetest--that is, Thou makest peace, or enterest into covenant with him (see on

). 
 
    rejoiceth and worketh--that is, who with joyful willingness worketh [GESENIUS] (
), but in Thy ways ("those"), namely, of covenant mercy to Thy people (
); on the strength of the everlasting continuance of His covenant they infer by faith, "we shall be saved." God "remembered" for them His covenant (
), though they often "remembered not" Him (
). CASTELLIO translates, "we have sinned for long in them ('thy ways'), and could we then be saved?" But they hardly would use such a plea when their very object was to be saved.

entries.title: Isaiah 64:6
segments:
6. unclean thing--legally unclean, as a leper. True of Israel, everywhere now cut off by unbelief and by God's judgments from the congregation of the saints. 
 
    righteousness--plural, "uncleanness" extended to every particular act of theirs, even to their prayers and praises. True of the best doings of the unregenerate (

). 
 
    filthy rags--literally, a "menstruous rag" (

). 
 
    fade ... leaf-- (

entries.title: Isaiah 64:10
segments: 10. holy cities--No city but Jerusalem is called "the holy city" (

); the plural, therefore, refers to the upper and the lower parts of the same city Jerusalem [VITRINGA]; or all Judea was holy to God, so its cities were deemed "holy" [MAURER]. But the parallelism favors VITRINGA. Zion and Jerusalem (the one city) answering to "holy cities."

entries.title: Isaiah 64:11
segments:
11. house--the temple. 
 
    beautiful--includes the idea of glorious (

). 
 
    burned-- (

). Its destruction under Nebuchadnezzar prefigured that under Titus. 
 
    pleasant things--Hebrew, "objects of desire"; our homes, our city, and all its dear associations.
